- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.2), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 10–15 day moving average of prior 10–15 prices.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early downward trend; if sentiment turns negative after 10 days, reduce forecast by 3–6% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to err on the high side; use 10–15% lower baseline for forecast unless sentiment confirms bullish momentum.
